chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yusuf ibn Ibrahim, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in a garment whose warp, buttons, and trimming are of silk; rather, only solid silk has been considered disliked for men.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or piece of clothing under discussion
key_terms.الْحَرِيرُ الْمُبْهَمُ: plain or entirely silk fabric without distinction
key_terms.حَرِيرًا: silk as a material in the garment
key_terms.سَدَاهُ: its warp, meaning one of the structural threads of the fabric
key_terms.عَلَمُهُ: its decorative trimming or marked edging
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection or harm in terms of legal permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for men to wear clothing that contains some silk?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning men's clothing, distinguishing between limited silk elements in a garment and a garment made wholly of silk. It indicates that minor silk components are not objectionable, while the disapproved form is undifferentiated full silk for men.
